title: Video by metromedia.house
description:
This photo has some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley before anyone knew who they were.

The kid next to Paul Graham is Sam Altman.

His first startup, Loopt, never became a huge consumer business, but it was eventually sold for $43 million. Altman later became president of Y Combinator, then went on to build OpenAI.

Steve Huffman almost didn’t get into YC at all.

His original idea was rejected, but Graham liked the founders enough to call them back and tell them to build something else.

That company became Reddit.

Then there was Justin Kan.

His first startup, a calendar app called Kiko, struggled once Google launched its own calendar. He sold the company on eBay, came back to YC, and his next company eventually became Twitch.

The people in this photo helped turn YC into something much bigger than an accelerator. It went on to back Airbnb, Stripe, DoorDash, Coinbase and thousands of other startups.

The PayPal Mafia became famous because a small group of people left one company and built some of Silicon Valley’s biggest businesses.

YC built a system for finding people like that before anyone knew who they were.
